note: The single source of the interview questions (PRD §3.12.8, Appendix F). Wording is the PRD's, word for word; `lead_in` is the interviewer's cue before the spoken question and `note` a label, both kept apart so transcripts are matched on the spoken wording. Priority `core`: never dropped when a guide is shortened (F.8 rule 6); `standard`: dropped first.
principles: Story before explanation. Ask what happened, not how it works. "How does it work?" gets the procedure; "What happened last time?" gets the practice.
Gather without judging. No analytical or evaluative questions early; collect what people actually decide and do, in their words.
Oblique before direct. For sensitive ground, ask for the story a new colleague should hear, not "what goes wrong".
Their words first. Note the SME's terms and reuse them in later questions ("the inefficient disconnect, as you call it"); never correct them.
"What happened next?" before "why?" Save "why" for the contrast movement (M6).
Silent listening. Don't fill pauses; the useful detail often follows one.
Follow a good story over the script. The close (M7) catches what's missed.
Documents last. Never mention the SOP's version before M6.
Present contrasts without evaluation. When playing back differences (M6, follow-ups, validation), describe them and let the SME draw the conclusion.
Session targets: at least three stories (went well, went badly, surprise); every decision deepened once; every handoff named; the timeline read back once; strengths as well as weaknesses.

opener.text: We're mapping the [end-to-end scope, e.g. from product planning to raw materials to supplier to logistics to customer fulfilment] for [business]. I understand your team plays a key role in [area], so [referrer role] suggested I speak with you to understand how it works from your perspective and where it fits in the broader chain. We're mapping how the work actually happens, not checking on anyone; nothing will be linked to your name.
opener.follow_up: Last time we covered [topics]; today I'd like to pick up where we left off.
opener.note: Use roles by default ("the global contract holder"); you may type personal names into your own copy. The guide is your working document and is never exported or sent anywhere.

movements.name: The last real case: the As done spine
Stories: prompting questions and the SME's own reading of them
Contrast: official vs lived; now bring the documents
Close: ask only what is still missing

questions.wording: Who are the core teams and individuals involved in [scope] from your side, and how are they structured?
probes: Who do they report to?
Global, regional or local?
questions.translation: Roles and lanes; reporting and global/regional notes

questions.wording: What activities does each of these teams manage?
probes: Which are the big ones by effort or risk?

questions.wording: How does your team interface with [adjacent functions]? Where do the handoffs happen?
probes: What passes across — a document, a decision, a request?
What happens when it's late or unclear?
questions.translation: Cross-lane edges with the information or artefact that passes; interface issues as constraints

questions.wording: Where do the key decision rights sit — who decides, who must be consulted, who is told?
probes: Does it always work that way?
questions.translation: Decisions and approvals with A, C, I; ownership mismatches

questions.wording: Could you help me separate the activities your team manages from those of [other team]? Where do they overlap or fall between the two?
probes: Who shows up to the supplier or customer?
Who is held accountable when it goes wrong?
questions.translation: Lane boundaries; overlaps and gaps flagged; shared delivery recorded as one Responsible plus Consulted, with a note

questions.wording: What capability — skills, ways of working, systems or process — do you see as the biggest strength in how this is managed today? And the biggest weakness?
probes: What should we keep no matter what?
Where does it hurt most?
questions.translation: Strengths to preserve and weaknesses to improve, each with a capability dimension (B.36); weaknesses also become constraints with a cause type

questions.wording: Where do you see the biggest risk in how this works today?
probes: What would it take for that to happen?
questions.translation: Risk notes linked to steps and cause types

questions.wording: Opener (F.3)
What should I call your role, and what do the people around you call this piece of work?
probes: Any nicknames for parts of it?
questions.translation: Role alias; SME terms to glossary

questions.wording: Tell me about a normal shift in this work.
probes: And then?
What's the busiest part?
How many of these in a day?
questions.translation: Phase candidates in SME names; frequency and volume

questions.wording: What makes a good day different from a bad day?
probes: What did a bad day look like last time?
questions.translation: Constraints with cause type; KPI candidates; fragments

questions.wording: If a new colleague joined tomorrow, what's the one thing you'd make sure they understood?
probes: What would they learn the hard way?

questions.wording: Think of the last time you did this from start to finish. What set it off?
probes: How did you find out?

questions.wording: Walk me through what happened, step by step, as it actually went.
probes: What happened next?
Who did that?
What did you have in front of you?
Where did it go after you?
targets: Flow (lived sequence, roles, handoffs, artefacts, systems)
questions.translation: Lived activities; explicit_order edges; cross-lane handoffs; artefacts in/out

questions.wording: Let me play back the order I heard: [list]. What did I get wrong or leave out?
probes: Anything in between you didn't mention?
If stuck, work backwards: "Just before you finished, what had to be true?"
questions.translation: Confirms or corrects edges; corrections outrank narration order

questions.wording: How long did each part take, and where were you waiting on someone or something?
probes: What were you waiting for?
Is that usual?
questions.translation: work_min / wait_min on the receiving step

questions.wording: How did you know you were done, and who got the result?
probes: What would they say if it was late or wrong?

questions.wording: Was that case typical? What was the same as usual, what was different, and what surprised you?
probes: What do you do instead when it's busy or something's missing?
questions.translation: Condition-based branch with the lived alternative, or typical responses for a complex step

questions.wording: Take me through this form. Who fills in each part, and when?
probes: Who uses it after that?
questions.translation: Activities anchored to the artefact; trace stances

questions.wording: What do you check here, and what happens if it's blank or wrong?
probes: Who fixes it?
How long does that add?

questions.wording: Where does this go next, and does anyone sign it?
probes: What if they're not around?

questions.wording: What happened on this one?
probes: What was different?

questions.wording: What decisions do you make daily? Weekly? Monthly? Once a year? Only when something unusual happens?
probes: However small
questions.translation: Decision list with cadence (B.37); chooses which to deepen (4–6 per session)

questions.wording: At that point, what were your options?
probes: Any you ruled out?

questions.wording: What information did you receive, and which of it did you actually pay attention to?
probes: What would have made you go the other way?
questions.translation: Criteria or signals watched; information in; work-type cues

questions.wording: Is there a rule for this, or does it depend? On what?
probes: How often does the rule not fit?
questions.translation: Rule-based vs judgment; clear / complicated / complex cue

questions.wording: Who has the final say, whose advice do you seek, and who do you tell?
probes: Who would you call if unsure?
questions.translation: Decider; A, C, I; advice network

questions.wording: What did you use — documents, screens, tools? (A) · What would someone need to learn to do this well? (S) · Do you have a rule of thumb? (H) · Was there a time that taught you how to handle this? (E) · Does this role need a particular knack? (N, role level only)
probes: Ask each once, in the SME's words

questions.wording: How is the decision communicated or put into action, and who picks it up?
probes: In what form — email, system, conversation?
questions.translation: Information out; downstream edge (used to stitch flows across interviews)

questions.wording: What information, if you had it, would make this decision better?
probes: Who has it today?
questions.translation: Information wanted; improvement signal (kept in the SME's voice)

questions.wording: What would a new joiner probably get wrong here? What if the usual person were away?
probes: What would you tell them?

questions.wording: Tell me about a time this went really well.
Tell me about a time it went badly, or nearly did.
Tell me about a time something surprised you.
What's a story people around here tell about this work?
Was that more like following a procedure, needing an expert, working it out as you went, or firefighting?
questions.translation: SME work-type signifier for the story

questions.wording: How often does something like that happen?
Who ended up deciding?
In that moment, did you have too little freedom to act, about the right amount, or too much?
What would you want more of, and less of, next time?
questions.translation: Improvement signals and strengths, in the SME's voice
questions.note: More Like This, Less Like That

questions.wording: Earlier you described [step] as [SME's words]. Is that how it's meant to work?
What does the procedure say here, as far as you know?
questions.translation: unknown_rule if the SME is unaware of the rule

questions.wording: What would happen if you followed it exactly, every time?
Why do people do it this way?
questions.translation: Stated reason → gap-class proposal and cause type

questions.wording: The procedure mentions [e.g. plan approval by the lead]. Where does that happen in practice?
What stops you doing this the way you'd like? And what makes it possible to do it well?
questions.translation: Governing vs enabling constraints; strengths to preserve

questions.wording: How do you know this went well — what's measured, and who looks at it?
Who signs off, who must be consulted, and who just gets told?
How long does the whole thing take, typically and at worst?
What systems or tools do you use along the way?
What should I have asked that I didn't?
Who else should I talk to about this?
Going back to where we left off, could you help me separate the activities managed by [your team] versus [other team]?
questions.built_from: Overlaps and boundary gaps from L5 or the map

questions.wording: You mentioned previously that [SME's own words, ≤ 20 words]. How do you manage that today, and where do you see the biggest risk?
questions.built_from: Verified quotes carrying constraints, risks or stated reasons

questions.wording: You mentioned there's unclarity around accountabilities between [role A] and [role B]. Where is it not working well — for example at handoffs?
On [activity], how does your team work with [other role's team]? It sounds like both show up together.
questions.translation: One Responsible plus Consulted; shared-delivery note

questions.wording: On [step], the map currently shows a gap between [A] and [B]. What happens in between?
[Validation question from the review workbench]

landscape.title: Landscape
landscape.who: Team leads, contract holders, cross-functional owners (one per stakeholder group lead)
landscape.purpose: The end-to-end picture: which teams, how structured, what each manages, interfaces and handoffs between them, where decision rights sit, capability strengths and weaknesses

sections.label: Role module (3–5 blank rows for the stakeholder group)
sections.note: Add 3–5 questions for this stakeholder group from the L3–L5 wording, naming its specific interfaces and decisions.

practice.title: Practice
practice.who: People who do the work (one per person)
practice.purpose: The workflow as actually performed: steps, decisions, know-how, variations, official vs lived

sections.label: M2 — The last real case: the As done spine
M3 — Artefact walk-through (with the completed examples)
M4 — Decisions: decision mapping and ASHEN
sections.note: Start with the M4.0 sweep, then deepen 4–6 decisions in process order with M4.1–M4.8; the rest go to a follow-up.

sections.label: M5 — Stories: prompting questions and the SME's own reading of them
M6 — Contrast: official vs lived; now bring the documents
M7 — Close: ask only what is still missing

follow_up.title: Follow-up
follow_up.purpose: Close gaps and test interpretations using the SME's own words

sections.label: Opener
sections.note: Use the short opener with the follow-up line.

sections.label: F-series with blank rows for reflective probes
sections.note: Reflective probes quote only verified claims, in the SME's own words (at most 20 words), never names of other people.

footer: Say or note the question ID (e.g. [M2.2]) when you ask it — it helps the app link each answer to its question. Use roles, not names.
